claims.statement: For row-generator Q with off-diagonal q_ij >= 0 and Q 1 = 0, mean counts x'=(Q^T+diag(r))x, total N=1^T x and composition p=x/N; a pure start e_i has p'_j(0)=q_ij for j != i and (d/dt)log N(0)=r_i.
assumptions: time-homogeneous rates during the observation window
r_i is net per-capita count growth (birth minus death)
x is a deterministic mean-count state or the exact mean trajectory, not a single stochastic sample path
absolute total counts are observed for the r_i identity
claims.status: established primary-literature result for equivalent mean branching-process interface; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Gunnarsson, Foo and Leder 2023 Proposition 1 identifies switching rates and net birth rates from pure-start mean-count derivatives; Proposition 2 identifies outgoing switching rates from pure-start mean-fraction derivatives. Their row matrix is the transpose convention used here.
claims.costs: K pure-state start conditions for direct initial-slope identification; absolute count measurements and biological replicates; fraction-only data cannot identify a common shift of all net growth rates.
claims.falsifier: Under the stated fixed-generator mean model and exact measurement, a mismatch in the algebraic derivative identities falsifies the implementation or model convention; empirical finite data need a separately specified noise model.
claims.next_gate: Do not pursue as a novelty claim; use only as a reconstruction baseline when evaluating a new rate-cap or control result.

claims.statement: If max_i sum_{j!=i}q_ij <= Lambda and max_i |r_i| <= R, then for a pure state e_i and tau>0, |p_j(tau)/tau-q_ij| <= (Lambda+R)(2Lambda+3R)tau for j!=i, and |log(N(tau)/N(0))/tau-r_i| <= R(Lambda+R)tau.
assumptions: constant Q and r over [0,tau]
deterministic mean ODE and exact endpoints
pure start e_i
uniform exit-rate and absolute net-growth caps
the observed total N remains positive
claims.status: internally proved conditional finite-time bias lemma; elementary ODE Lipschitz estimate; novelty UNKNOWN
claims.novelty_boundary: Primary literature already treats finite-time noisy observations by likelihood fitting; this report did not establish priority or show that the elementary secant bound improves those estimators.
claims.costs: Endpoint measurement errors eta_p and eta_l add eta_p/tau and eta_l/tau to the deterministic radii; statistical sampling, purity, rate-cap acquisition, and biological-unit replication are extra costs.
claims.falsifier: For known valid caps and controlled measurement error, a held-out mean trajectory whose secants violate the bound rejects at least one model/cap/error premise.
claims.next_gate: Compare against likelihood-based estimates on a pre-registered branching-process simulation and a held-out in-vitro dataset; test conditioning and coverage rather than only algebraic bias.

claims.statement: K pure starts are minimal for identifying all K(K-1) off-diagonal switching rates and K net-growth rates from t=0 composition and log-total derivatives alone, for an unrestricted open rate family.
assumptions: only first derivatives at time zero are observed
unknown parameters are all off-diagonal q_ij and all r_i, with no known sparsity or parameter sharing
each tested initial condition yields K-1 independent composition slopes and one total-count slope
claims.novelty_boundary: This is an observation-budget qualification, not a universal minimum on the number of cultures or starts; full trajectories, sparsity, shared parameters, or auxiliary observables change the answer.
claims.costs: At least K derivative-probe experiments by dimension for this unrestricted t=0 interface; experiment count multiplies by action levels and biological replicates.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample within the stated unrestricted t=0-only interface with fewer than K experiments and injective parameter map would falsify the dimension argument; the stated assumptions make fewer than K times K scalar measurements impossible for an open K^2-dimensional family.
claims.next_gate: When reducing starts, state which additional time-course or structural information supplies the missing rank.

claims.statement: K starts are not necessary from full continuous exact count trajectories: in the two-state model, a single pure-start trajectory from e_1 with q_12=a>0 identifies a, b, r_1, and r_2; more generally a cyclic initial state with full Krylov rank yields a full-span state curve and identifies A.
assumptions: exact noiseless absolute count trajectory and its derivatives
known initial state and fixed autonomous matrix A
for the two-state construction, a>0 so the second state becomes populated
for the general statement, the initial vector is cyclic for A
claims.status: internally proved structural counterexample to unconditional K-start minimality; finite-data conditioning UNKNOWN
claims.novelty_boundary: This refutes only unconditional minimality; the standard cyclic-vector observability condition and structural exact-data scope are not a biological or practical acquisition claim.
claims.costs: Continuous exact trajectory and derivatives are an idealization; state-spanning can be ill-conditioned, particularly when transition rates are small or states are rarely occupied.
claims.falsifier: The explicit two-state formulas fail if applied to an exact trajectory satisfying a>0 and x_2(t)>0; with noisy finite data, the issue is estimator error rather than structural injectivity.
claims.next_gate: Quantify conditioning and sample cost before using fewer sorted starting populations.

claims.statement: For a finite action menu with per-action Metzler mean matrices enclosed entrywise by A_u^- <= A_u <= A_u^+, positive comparison propagates componentwise state intervals; interval ratios plus a composition-speed margin give a conservative finite-grid reach-avoid certificate for every schedule enumerated on that fixed grid.
assumptions: piecewise-constant action and time-constant unknown A_u within each action use
nonnegative initial counts and Metzler A_u
joint confidence region actually contains the unknown action matrices with stated coverage
uniform switching-exit cap Lambda and net-growth cap R for the continuous-time path margin
unsafe constraint is current composition occupancy unless a first-hit lineage-history state is explicitly added
numerical matrix exponentials are outward-certified
objective and unsafe events are defined on phenotype compositions/mean counts
claims.status: internally reconstructed conservative certificate algorithm; no efficient-complexity or biological validation claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Cell-state/cancer schedule optimization is prior art; the possible narrower addition is an explicit interval-confidence safe schedule certificate, whose novelty and value are UNKNOWN. Rejected schedules do not prove unreachability.
claims.costs: Entrywise confidence-set construction; exponential matrix calculations and certified rounding; exhaustive search O(|U|^M); time-grid conservatism; cell/action/replicate/exposure measurement; stochastic path-risk analysis not included.
claims.falsifier: A feasible true matrix outside a claimed enclosure or a trajectory outside its propagated state interval falsifies the implementation; failed certification alone is not falsification of physical reachability.
claims.next_gate: Implement interval arithmetic on a small benchmark and compare its safe schedules and false-rejection rate with exact worst-case search over synthetic compact parameter sets.

claims.statement: The mean-population switching model and finite-grid reach-avoid certificate do not establish individual-cell reprogramming, regeneration, stochastic path safety, or clinical safety.
assumptions: phenotype labels, target/unsafe classes, and the mean-rate model would have to be acquired for a named protocol
branching noise, cell heterogeneity, state-age effects, exposure uncertainty, and washout outcomes are outside the certificate
claims.status: principled scope obstruction; biological claim UNKNOWN
claims.novelty_boundary: A model-conditional composition result is not a natural-law or regenerative-outcome claim.
claims.costs: Lineage tracing, sorted-state purity, total counts, phenotype assays, measured intracellular exposure, biological-unit replication, post-washout follow-up, and rare-event bounds.
claims.falsifier: A held-out assay can reject the fitted model or policy prediction; no such biological dataset was acquired in this lane.
claims.next_gate: Acquire context-specific longitudinal lineage/exposure data and a separate stochastic safety model before asserting a biological controller.
